name: LM4990ITLX_NOPB
title: LM4990: 2 W bridged audio power amplifier with selectable shutdown polarity
summary: A mono audio power amplifier with a bridged (BTL) output for phones and other portable products, running from 2.2 V to 5.5 V. From 5 V it gives 1.25 W into 8 Ω, or 2 W into 4 Ω in the WSON and exposed-pad MSOP packages, at 1% THD+N. Gain is set by two external resistors and the part is unity-gain stable; no output coupling, bootstrap or snubber parts are needed. Shutdown draws 0.1 µA typical, and on the 10-pin packages its active level is chosen by a pin. LM4990ITLX/NOPB is the 9-bump DSBGA on a 3000-piece reel.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: Stress beyond these ratings can damage the part; the operating ratings are where it is meant to work, with performance held only inside the electrical tables.

In shutdown with VDD above 6 V (up to 8 V), most of the extra current runs through the ESD structures; a source that limits it to 10 mA keeps the part safe. Enabled between 5.5 V and 6.5 V the part is not damaged but its life is shortened; above 6.5 V with no current limit it is destroyed.

Allowed dissipation is the lower of the internal limit and PDMAX = (TJMAX − TA)/θJA, so it falls as ambient rises; the peak dissipation comes at an output power well below full output (peak power dissipation equation, or the dissipation curves).
Human body model: 100 pF through 1.5 kΩ. Machine model: 220 pF to 240 pF into every pin.
The DSBGA figure assumes every bump is connected; all bumps carry heat equally.

The WSON figures are for the exposed pad tied to GND or to isolated copper: on the LM4990LD demo board, 2.02 mm × 14.86 mm (86.7 mil × 585 mil) on the top layer and 13.97 mm × 18.03 mm (550 mil × 710 mil) on the bottom layer.
Soldering: TI application report AN-1187.

circuits.title: Typical audio amplifier application (NGZ and DGQ)
circuits.description: A single-ended audio signal reaches -IN through Ci and Ri; Rf from VO1 back to -IN sets the bridge gain at 2 × Rf/Ri, which is 2 with these values. +IN sits on the BYPASS node, held at half supply and filtered by CB. The 8 Ω speaker hangs between VO1 and VO2 with no coupling capacitor. Two control lines set SHUTDOWN and SD MODE; the part turns off when they agree. CS decouples VDD.
notes: The audio source returns to GND.

circuits.title: Typical audio amplifier application (YZR and DGK)
circuits.description: The same bridge amplifier for the parts without SD MODE: Ci and Ri into -IN, Rf from VO1 for a gain of 2, +IN on the CB-filtered BYPASS node, the speaker across VO1 and VO2, CS on VDD. One control line drives SHUTDOWN, active low.

circuits.title: Higher gain audio amplifier
circuits.description: For closed-loop differential gains above 10, C4 across the feedback resistor R3 limits the bandwidth and stops high-frequency oscillation. The input runs through C2 and R2 into -IN; +IN and C3 sit on BYPASS. R1 pulls SHUTDOWN up and jumper J1 grounds it; R4 pulls SD MODE down and jumper J2 lifts it to VDD. C1 decouples VDD and the 8 Ω speaker bridges VO1 and VO2.

parts.note: feedback capacitor; 25 pF with R3 = 20 kΩ gives a −3 dB point near 320 kHz
feedback resistor; sets the gain with R2

notes: R3 and C4 must be chosen so that their corner stays above 20 kHz.

circuits.title: Differential amplifier configuration
circuits.description: A balanced input drives both amplifier inputs. One leg enters -IN through C2 and R2, with R3 back from VO1; the other enters +IN through C4 and R5, and R6 ties +IN to the half-supply BYPASS node filtered by C3. The jumper and pull resistors on SHUTDOWN and SD MODE, C1 on VDD and the 8 Ω bridged speaker are as in the higher gain circuit.

circuits.title: Reference design board
circuits.description: The evaluation board: the higher gain circuit with R3 = 20 kΩ and C4 not fitted. Audio enters through C2 and R2; BYPASS and +IN share C3; R1, J1, R4 and J2 set the shutdown input and polarity; C1 decouples VDD; the speaker sits across VO1 and VO2.

operation.text: Inside are two op amps. The first has its gain set by external Ri and Rf; the second is fixed as an inverter of gain −1 by two 20 kΩ resistors and is driven from the first one's output. VO1 and VO2 therefore move in antiphase with equal amplitude and the load is driven differentially. For a given supply this doubles the voltage swing and gives four times the power of a single-ended stage, unclipped and not current limited. Both outputs rest at half supply, so no DC appears across the load and no output coupling capacitor is used.

Two output stages in one package dissipate up to four times as much as a single-ended amplifier; the peak power dissipation equation or the dissipation curves give the peak. Junction temperature must stay under 150 °C. Extra copper on the leads, best of all on VDD, GND and the outputs, lowers the thermal resistance below its free-air value. If the junction would still run too hot, lower the supply, raise the load impedance or reduce the ambient temperature. The WSON exposed pad is tied to GND or isolated copper (the LM4990LD board uses 2.02 × 14.86 mm on top and 13.97 × 18.03 mm on the bottom). The 4 Ω rating at 5 V needs WSON or exposed-DAP MSOP with the pad on a thermal plane.

Good bypassing matters for low noise and high PSRR. The capacitors on VDD and on BYPASS go as near the part as possible. A 5 V regulator with its own 10 µF tantalum or electrolytic and a ceramic does not remove the need for local bypassing at the LM4990. The CB value is a trade between PSRR, click and pop, cost and size.

Shutdown switches off the bias circuits, leaving about 0.1 µA. On NGZ and DGQ the SD MODE pin picks the polarity: tied to VDD the part is shutdown-high, tied to GND shutdown-low; the part is off whenever SHUTDOWN and SD MODE are at the same level. DGK and YZR are shutdown-low only. The switching thresholds are in the electrical tables and the hysteresis curves. Drive SHUTDOWN fully to ground or to supply: levels in between still disable the part but may draw more than 0.1 µA. Never leave it floating; a microcontroller output works, or a single-throw switch with a pull-up or pull-down resistor.

The amplifier is unity-gain stable. Low gain keeps THD+N down and signal-to-noise up, at the cost of a larger input signal; codecs commonly supply 1 Vrms or more. With a closed-loop differential gain above 10, a feedback capacitor across Rf may be needed to limit the bandwidth and prevent high-frequency oscillation, chosen so the roll-off stays above 20 kHz; 20 kΩ with 25 pF puts the corner near 320 kHz.

Ci and Ri form a first-order high-pass that sets the low-frequency limit. Small speakers in portable products seldom reproduce much below 100 Hz to 150 Hz, so a large Ci adds cost and size for little gain. A large Ci also needs more charge, drawn from the output through the feedback path, to reach its half-supply resting voltage, which makes a pop at turn-on more likely; sizing Ci only as large as the low-frequency response needs keeps pops down.

CB governs how quickly the outputs ramp to half supply at turn-on, and a slower ramp gives a smaller pop. Pairing a 1.0 µF CB with a Ci of 0.1 µF to 0.39 µF makes shutdown and turn-on practically free of clicks and pops. A 0.1 µF CB still gives stable operation, with no oscillation or motorboating, but turn-on clicks become much more likely; 1.0 µF is the recommended CB outside the most cost-driven designs. Wake-up time is about 100 ms at 5 V.

Find the minimum supply for the wanted power from the output power against supply voltage curves; headroom above it lets peaks pass without audible clipping. Check the dissipation for that supply and load. Set the gain from the minimum differential gain equation and split it into Ri and Rf from the input impedance wanted. Place the −3 dB corners five times beyond the band edges, then size Ci from Ri and the low corner, and confirm AVD × fH sits well below the 2.5 MHz gain-bandwidth product.

ESD protection is limited: store and handle the part with its leads shorted or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates. In shutdown with VDD between 6 V and 8 V, the excess current flows through the ESD structures and the part survives if the source limits it to 10 mA. Running enabled between 5.5 V and 6.5 V shortens life without immediate damage; above 6.5 V with no current limit the part is destroyed.
